findings.claim: square brackets in a title broke the index entry
accented letters were dropped from the slug
a newline in the description broke the index line
r1 did not assert each kind's path and title
the bracket test never checks that kmctl new succeeded or that the file is listed, so it passes when new refuses or crashes on the title

verdict.text: All four round-1 findings are fixed and the fixes broke nothing I could find.
One small new gap: the bracket test passes even if `kmctl new` fails, because `kmctl check` passes on an empty bundle.
That is a one-line test fix, so the label is fix.
Ran `loopctl gate stamp` in the worktree: lint, format, tests and rows r1 to r5 pass, stamp green 170b33b90585fcb1bd80fbda8cc827134b0796362ee10e32b15009cf3ae620aa.
Read src/kmctl/concepts.py and tests/test_new_concept.py in full, and the `_ENTRY` regex in checks.py.

Probed in a scratch repo with the worktree's kmctl: practice 'Use [WIP] flags (x)' with a two-line description wrote `- [Use (WIP) flags (x)](use-wip-flags-x.md): a b`, and the front matter title kept the brackets.
Decision 'Café ]weird[' became 0001-cafe-weird.md with link text 'ADR 0001: Café )weird('.
kmctl check passed on both.
r1's test now asserts the path and front matter title for every kind, which covers "misnamed" in its fails_when.
f1: resolved.
`_link_text` at concepts.py:64 turns brackets into parentheses in the link text only.
Parentheses inside the brackets do not trip `_ENTRY`, and the probe passed kmctl check.
f2: resolved.
concepts.py:54 folds with NFKD before slugging, tested by test_new_title_with_accents_keeps_its_letters.
f3: resolved.
concepts.py:150 collapses all whitespace, so the index entry and front matter stay on one line, with a test.
f4: resolved.
test_new_creates_each_kind checks every kind's path and title.
f5: open, non-blocking.
test_new_title_with_brackets_stays_listed should assert `_new(...).exit_code == 0` and that the entry is in practices/index.md.
Without that, a regression where new refuses bracketed titles would still pass.
Non-blocking because the fix is a plain extra assertion I trust without a second look; the code it guards is correct today.
